topic: Hankel-history irregularity frontier for heterogeneous carryover effects in continuous reversible fixed-T panels. Under the time-invariant random-coefficient distributed-lag model, a fixed stayer-plus-full-dimensional-mover class, and explicitly bounded density, moment, eligibility and frontier-compatible semialgebraic tube constants, derive each lag's target-active pseudo-inverse leverage tail from the complete joint stratification of Hankel rank loss, maximal-minor contact and target-kernel alignment. Prove the induced regular, critical and irregular matched minimax squared-risk and shortest uniformly honest expected-confidence-length regimes; construct a feasible joint-Gamma trimmed/debiased estimator with geometry-estimated cutoff attaining the upper bound and prove a matching lower bound. Recover finite-support/root-G and scalar slow-mover cases. Use the Gentzkow-Shapiro-Sinkinson/dist_lag_het consumer.

open_problems.open_problem: Target-active Hankel tail atlas: determine every lag-specific pseudo-inverse leverage tail in continuous fixed-T panels by jointly stratifying Hankel rank loss, maximal-minor contact order, and target-kernel alignment, including logarithmic multiplicities, multi-rank intersections, target-inactive strata, and support-boundary tangencies.

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies each mean lag coefficient through a Moore-Penrose score; outside finite treatment support it expects non-root-G behavior, proposes leverage trimming, and says cutoff choice is delicate.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The distributed-lag paper reduces the continuous-support problem to a coordinate-specific Moore-Penrose norm but does not classify its tail, while the repository contains separate CAD, minor-rank, and scalar-annihilator ideas without a probability-tube theorem. Generic random-matrix results do not apply because every Hankel entry repeats one of only T-1 increments; generic algebraic tube bounds miss higher-order contact and boundary tangency; and smallest-singular-value analysis alone misclassifies rank-loss points where e_k is orthogonal to the vanishing right-kernel direction. The presolve's smooth corank-one comparison and generic codimension calculation therefore cover only one stratum, not the required uniform atlas.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite boundary-compatible Whitney/CAD or resolution stratification with, on every eligible stratum, explicit α_k, m_k and uniform positive constants c_k,C_k such that c_k u^(-α_k)(log u)^(m_k) ≤ P(H_k>u) ≤ C_k u^(-α_k)(log u)^(m_k), together with target-inactivity criteria and a symbolic K=1,T=5 local calculation showing u²P(H_k>u) converges to a finite positive constant for k=0,1 near (1,-1,1,-1).

writing_exemplar.why: It states the exact heterogeneous distributed-lag consumer, derives the lag-specific pseudo-inverse identifying score, and isolates the continuous-support cutoff problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: complex reversible treatments obscure individual lag effects -> time-invariant random coefficients recover lag-specific means -> continuous histories create unresolved target-specific inverse-leverage tails

method_exemplars.technique: Use the algebraic structure and singular loci of Hankel determinantal ideals to enumerate rank and contact strata before adding target-alignment equations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired tail atlas is supported on a Hankel linear section of a determinantal variety, so its rank-loss skeleton is exactly the structured object this paper studies.

method_exemplars.technique: Principalize the joint minor/alignment ideal and read tail powers and logarithmic multiplicities from local monomial exponents and Jacobians.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A resolution chart turns coordinate-specific pseudo-inverse blow-up into the monomial sublevel-set problem needed for the stated two-sided tail law.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate inverse-design divergence into trimming, bias correction, and a nonstandard asymptotic distribution in a correlated random-coefficient panel.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the econometric bridge from an inverse-design tail to estimability once the new Hankel geometry determines that tail.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Inverse-weight papers establish that tails can change rates, but here the tail itself is generated by dependent polynomial minors and may differ by lag through target alignment. The prior weak-overlap proposal explicitly left its Le Cam/Assouad converse incomplete, while the weak-rank bank warns that union-honest length can be governed by a least-favorable mixture rather than every pairwise modulus. A valid converse must perturb conditional coefficient means only inside boundary-compatible tubes while preserving the fixed stayer-plus-full-dimensional-mover class, the Γ moment, eligibility eigenvalues, density bounds, and q moments; joint inference must also account for several lags sharing the same histories and rank strata.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit phase diagram indexed by each resolved pair (α_k,m_k) and debiasing order, with matching upper and Le Cam/Assouad or fuzzy-hypothesis lower bounds for lagwise and joint squared risk, plus a between-stratum modulus or finite-mixture dual that gives the minimum worst-case expected length of uniformly honest lag intervals or simultaneous confidence regions, including exact critical logarithms and any unavoidable adaptation factor.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation ties inverse-weight identification directly to nonregular rates and organizes the question by tail regimes.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: identification uses extreme inverse weights -> their tails destroy regular estimation -> a matched rate and inference frontier is required

method_exemplars.technique: Compute a modulus of continuity for the lag-mean functional and turn it into matched minimax risk lower and upper bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the Hankel tube experiment is embedded, the target is a linear functional observed through an ill-conditioned operator, exactly the structural form handled by optimal recovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Use between-class and ordered moduli, including composite mixtures, to lower-bound and construct honest intervals by expected length.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested interval must cover a union of regular, critical, and irregular Hankel strata while its length is evaluated within each stratum.

method_exemplars.technique: Add an explicit worst-case trimming-bias bound to the stochastic radius and optimize the resulting honest confidence length.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unresolved Hankel tube creates a deterministic bias allowance analogous to the smoothness-class bias in their optimal interval construction.

open_problems.open_problem: Feasible joint-Γ adaptation: construct a cross-fitted trimmed and frontier-debiased estimator whose cutoff is learned from observed Hankel rank/contact/alignment geometry and whose lagwise and simultaneous inference remains honest when the tail exponent, active stratum, alignment order, and common Γ are unknown.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing slow-mover corrections expand around one scalar denominator, whereas a Hankel score can approach several intersecting minor surfaces and can cancel when the target becomes kernel-inactive. The distributed-lag paper leaves the continuous-treatment cutoff unresolved, and plugging a separately estimated Γ into a score multiplied by H_k can make the Γ remainder first order in the irregular regimes unless the equations are jointly orthogonalized. The repository's spectral review also requires an explicit rank-strength testing scale, while its switchback review shows that a selector depending on counterfactual outcomes is not feasible; here every geometry diagnostic and bias bound must be measurable from observed treatment histories and outcomes on training folds.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A measurable cross-fitted procedure combining a regular projector equation for Γ, smoothly clipped Moore-Penrose lag scores, chartwise local-polynomial or series corrections in resolved minor/alignment coordinates, and a data-chosen cutoff; its result would be a uniform oracle inequality, a joint influence expansion incorporating Γ and geometry estimation, and bias-aware or self-normalized lagwise and simultaneous confidence regions attaining the applicable risk and expected-length frontier up to a proved unavoidable adaptation cost.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the exact practical problem: a simple estimator under finite support gives way to a bias-variance cutoff choice under continuous histories.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: finite histories permit tuning-free lag estimation -> continuous histories create large pseudo-inverse scores -> feasible geometry-aware trimming and joint-Γ correction are needed

method_exemplars.technique: Lift smooth trimming and local-polynomial trimming-bias correction from a scalar ratio to chartwise coordinates of the principalized Hankel minor/alignment ideal.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest feasible bias-corrected estimator for a target preserved after trimming a small-denominator region.

method_exemplars.technique: Stack determinant-trimmed random-coefficient moments with the common-parameter equation and track the generated-regressor contribution in the asymptotic expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It connects scalar trimming technology to the same correlated random-coefficient panel architecture used by the destination problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert a declared uniform post-debias remainder bound into a worst-case-bias-aware critical value and optimize cutoff-specific length.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A data-chosen irregular cutoff needs coverage that remains valid when the remaining tube bias is bounded rather than assumed negligible.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Finite support separates every used history from problematic leverage values, whereas a full-dimensional continuous mover law places observations arbitrarily close to the Hankel rank locus; the literature analyzes these endpoints but not an experiment in which support mesh, stayer mass, and sample size move together. Prior panel proposals also warn that a claimed reduction must be literal and that rank-deficient histories require their own validity statement. The missing transition matters for the Gentzkow-Shapiro-Sinkinson consumer because newspaper counts are discrete but finely heterogeneous, so dist_lag_het lacks a principled diagnostic for when finite-support root-G inference approximates the continuous critical or irregular regime.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A triangular-array limit experiment indexed by support mesh δ_G, stayer mass π_G, and the oracle continuous-design cutoff h*_k(G), with explicit risk and limit laws when δ_G/h*_k(G) tends to infinity, a positive finite constant, or zero; the endpoint corollaries would recover the finite-support cell-mean/root-G formula, K=0 Graham-Powell/Sasaki-Ura slow movers, fixed-gap regularity, and each K≥1 target-active or target-inactive Hankel branch, together with an implementable dist_lag_het regime diagnostic.

writing_exemplar.why: It places the finite-support and continuous-support estimators side by side and supplies the exact empirical consumer, making the missing transition visible.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: finite-valued treatments permit simple root-G estimation -> continuous histories require leverage trimming -> support refinement needs a unified asymptotic regime map for practice

method_exemplars.technique: Use fixed-T random-coefficient moment identification to keep the target constant while only the support mesh and stayer mixture vary.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It separates identification of coefficient features from the new triangular-array strength calculation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use slow-mover trimming and nonstandard-rate asymptotics as the continuous scalar endpoint of the lattice-to-tube experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The K=0 chart of the Hankel transition must reproduce this established irregular-panel experiment.

method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest scalar benchmark for the joint limit in which stayer mass vanishes as mover support fills in.

literature_map:
Graham and Powell (2012, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA8220) is the irregular correlated-random-coefficient panel anchor: inverse within-unit designs identify means but create trimming bias and nonstandard rates.
Khan and Tamer (2010, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA7372) supplies the broader result that point identification through extreme inverse weights need not permit regular estimation.
Sasaki and Ura (2022, Econometric Theory, DOI 10.1017/S0266466621000025) gives the closest smooth-trimming and local bias-correction technology, but for a scalar denominator.
Sasaki and Ura (2026, Econometric Theory, DOI 10.1017/S0266466625100157; arXiv:2110.12041) unifies stayers and many slow movers without structured Hankel codimension or target alignment.
Arellano and Bonhomme (2012, ReStud, DOI 10.1093/restud/rdr045) anchors fixed-T identification of random-coefficient features.
de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfœuille (2025, arXiv:2508.07808) is the immediate consumer: finite-support distributed lags are root-G, while non-finite support requires a delicate leverage cutoff.
Their time-invariance restriction keeps the common Γ identified through projector moments even where lag-specific Moore-Penrose scores are irregular.
Conca, Mostafazadehfard, Singh, and Varbaro (2018, Advances in Mathematics) describe Hankel determinantal singularities but not real probability tubes or coordinate-specific leverage.
Wongkew (1993) and Demmel (1987) connect algebraic tubes and ill-conditioning; their global bounds do not supply target cancellation, sharp lower constants, or logarithmic multiplicities.
Dinh and Pham (2017) give polynomial-matrix Łojasiewicz bounds useful for envelopes, while Phong and Sturm (2000) offer a resolution/local-zeta route to exact powers and logarithms.
Donoho (1994), Low (1997), Cai and Low (2004), and Armstrong and Kolesár (2018) provide minimax-risk and honest expected-length machinery absent from the panel papers.
The verified source-paper boundary is sharper than a generic continuous-treatment extension: de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfœuille explicitly states the pseudo-inverse score, finite-support simplification, expected non-root-G behavior, and delicate cutoff choice.
The presolve K=1,T=4 exponent-one calculation and K=1,T=5 exponent-two early-kill check turn the missing codimension/contact/alignment theory into a falsifiable program rather than a slogan.
Gentzkow, Shapiro, and Sinkinson (2011, AER, DOI 10.1257/aer.101.7.2980) and dist_lag_het supply the applied endpoint where discrete counts, reversals, carryover, heterogeneity, and leverage diagnostics meet.
